Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, attached is a first-pass outline of reserved-capacity options tailored to Helio's projected inference footprint. The two questions we'd like to align on before a formal term sheet:

1) Target utilization profile over the commit (how much of the pool you expect to consume month-to-month; seasonal peaks okay).
2) Appetite for tenor tradeoffs (shorter term = smaller discount but more flexibility; longer term = deeper discount but more obligation).

Attached: reserved_terms_v1.pdf and pricing_scenarios.xlsx (three scenario breakdowns). High level we think there are three sensible sizing approaches depending on your tolerance for elasticity / buyback flexibility:
- Buffer-light (tight sizing, 12-month): smaller upfront commitment, lower discount, higher overage rates.
- Buffer-moderate (24-month): balanced commit with a 10–15% headroom recommendation.
- Buffer-heavy (36-month): larger commit with stepped discounts and a GPU-price protection clause.

One open item I want to flag up-front: GPU market cost volatility. Helio asked about a pass-through for material market price shocks — we've included an illustrative trigger in the spreadsheet but we'll need to agree guardrails (threshold % change, cap, and notice period).

Can we book a 30-minute call Thursday to run the scenarios with your procurement and finance teams? I penciled in a slot at 11:00 PT — happy to move.

Thanks,

Sanjay / team —

Thanks, Sanjay. I pulled the scenarios into a single sheet and added three market-stress columns as requested (0%, +10%, +20%). Attaching pricing_scenarios.xlsx. TL;DR of the commercial options: 

Scenario A — 12-month (Conservative)
- Commitment: 60 GPU-month equivalents / month
- Discount vs list: 18%
- Overages: 1.35x on-demand
- No buyback; mid-term upsizing allowed with pro-rata credit

Scenario B — 24-month (Balanced)
- Commitment: 90 GPU-month equivalents / month
- Discount vs list: 28%
- Overages: 1.20x on-demand
- 10% annual conversion option from committed -> reserved credits (one-time)

Scenario C — 36-month (Aggressive)
- Commitment: 120 GPU-month equivalents / month
- Discount vs list: 38% initial, step-down to 34% if utilization < 65% for any 2Q rolling window
- Overages: 1.10x on-demand
- Optional structured buyback (subject to separate schedule)
- GPU-market protection clause (illustrative): if market GPU procurement cost index moves up > 15% vs baseline, Redwood may propose a surcharge capped at +8% of committed monthly charge or offer credits in lieu of surcharge; customer to be notified 45 days in advance.

We put the fiscal math into the sheet with annualized committed $ and the +10/+20% stress columns. For Helio's modeling, the incremental delta between Scenario B and C at +20% market stress is ~18% of annual spend; that is, deeper commits buy you downside insulation but expose both parties to residual market shock risk.

I'll flag a couple of approval notes for internal ops/finance: anything > 35% discount or 36-month terms with buyback require finance escalation. Marissa, can you confirm escalation path and whether we can offer the structured buyback as standard or strategic?

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Reviewed Ben's scenarios. Quick internal guidance from Finance: 

• Approval thresholds: any proposal with an expected committed ARR > $3M or any single-year effective discount > 35% must be routed to the CFO for approval.
• 36-month tenors that include buyback or price protection mechanics are considered strategic and require VP Finance + Legal sign-off.
• Proposed market-protection surcharge cap of +8% is reasonable for an initial clause but we need a clear index and reconciliation cadence in the contract (monthly index, quarterly reconciles).

Suggested play: present Scenario B (24 months) as our recommended default commercial route for Helio — cleaner approval path, meaningful savings, and a modest conversion option that limits downside for both sides. For Scenario C, prepare an exec slide that quantifies worst-case exposure at +20% and include a proposed escrow/credit mechanism to offset underutilization claims.

Rishi — can Legal draft a short market-volatility clause and a buyback term stub? Also confirm whether the step-down discount language Ben suggested is enforceable without complex measurement points.
